source.text: וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִלְּבַד֙ הָרָעָ֣ב הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בִּימֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ יִצְחָ֛ק אֶל־אֲבִימֶּ֥לֶךְמֶֽלֶךְ־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים גְּרָֽרָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in [the] days of Abraham. And went Isaac to Abimelech, king of [the] Philistines, to Gerar.

en.L: And there was a famine in the land, besides the earlier famine that had been in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
en.B: Famine came to the land again, a second one after the famine of Abraham's time, and Isaac went to Gerar, to Abimelech king of the Philistines.
en.R: Once again there was a famine in the land, like the one in Abraham's time. So Isaac went to the town of Gerar, to Abimelech, the king of the Philistines.

decisions.choice: the earlier famine: the famine of 12:10
decisions.reason: In that famine Abraham went down to Egypt (12:10). Isaac's story now follows his father's: famine, a foreign king, a wife passed off as a sister (verse 7).

decisions.choice: Abimelech king of the Philistines: a ruler in the land Abraham had known
alternatives: the same Abimelech as in chapter 20
decisions.reason: Abraham dealt with an Abimelech of Gerar (20:2; 21:22). Many decades have passed, so this may be a son or successor with the same name or throne name. The people of Gerar are called Philistines, the name of the people best known in the land in later times (21:32).

source.text: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל־תֵּרֵ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה שְׁכֹ֣ן בָּאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And appeared to him YHWH and said, do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land that I will say to you.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him and said, "Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land of which I tell you.
en.B: There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Isaac and said, "Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in whatever land I name to you.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Isaac and said, "Do not go down to Egypt. Stay in the land I show you.

decisions.choice: do not go down to Egypt: Isaac is to stay in the promised land
decisions.reason: Abraham went down to Egypt in his famine (12:10). Isaac, the son once laid on the altar (22:2), never leaves the land; God keeps him in it.

decisions.choice: the land of which I tell you: words like those of the first call
decisions.reason: The words recall God's call to Abraham, "to the land I will show you" (12:1), and "on one of the mountains I will tell you of" (22:2).

source.text: גּ֚וּר בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶֽהְיֶ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ וַאֲבָרְכֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־לְךָ֣ וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֗ אֶתֵּן֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָֽאֲרָצֹ֣ת הָאֵ֔ל וַהֲקִֽמֹתִי֙ אֶת־הַשְּׁבֻעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם אָבִֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and I will bless you; for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath that I swore to Abraham your father.

en.L: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you, for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath that I swore to Abraham your father.
en.B: Stay on in this land as a resident foreigner, and I will be with you and bless you. It is to you and your descendants that I will give all these territories, and I will make good the oath I swore to your father Abraham.
en.R: Live in this land for now, and I will be with you and bless you. I will give all these lands to you and your descendants. I will keep the promise I made to your father Abraham with an oath.

decisions.choice: sojourn: live as a resident foreigner
decisions.reason: The verb (gur) means to live in a place without the rights of a native, as Abraham did in Gerar (20:1) and among the Hittites (23:4).

decisions.choice: I will be with you: God's presence promised
decisions.reason: This is the first time in Genesis God says these words to one of the patriarchs. He says them again to Isaac (verse 24) and to Jacob (28:15; 31:3). Abimelech himself sees it (verse 28).

decisions.choice: the oath I swore to Abraham: the oath of 22:16
decisions.reason: After Abraham offered Isaac, God swore by himself to bless him and multiply his offspring (22:16-18). Verses 3-5 repeat that oath to Isaac.

decisions.choice: offspring (L), descendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (zera) is "seed"; as in earlier chapters, Literal says "offspring" and Balanced and Readable say "descendants".

source.text: וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֤י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּכוֹכְבֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנָתַתִּ֣י לְזַרְעֲךָ֔ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הָאֲרָצֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑ל וְהִתְבָּרֲכ֣וּ בְזַרְעֲךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will multiply your offspring like [the] stars of the heavens, and I will give to your offspring all these lands; and will be blessed in your offspring all [the] nations of the earth,

en.L: And I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens and will give to your offspring all these lands; and in your offspring all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,
en.B: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and give them all these lands, and through your descendants every nation on earth will find blessing,
en.R: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give them all these lands. Through your descendants, all the nations of the earth will be blessed.

decisions.choice: shall be blessed in your offspring: blessing reaches the nations through Isaac's line
alternatives: shall bless themselves by your offspring (shall pray to be blessed as they are)
decisions.reason: The verb form here (hitbarakhu) is usually reflexive, "bless themselves": the nations would say "may God bless us as he blessed them". This translation reads it with the passive of 12:3 and 18:18, as the Septuagint does and as the New Testament quotes the parallel promise (Acts 3:25 quoting 22:18). On either reading the nations' blessing is bound up with Abraham's offspring.

decisions.choice: like the stars of the heavens: the promise of 15:5 and 22:17
decisions.reason: God had told Abraham to count the stars if he could (15:5) and repeated the picture in his oath (22:17).

source.text: עֵ֕קֶב אֲשֶׁר־שָׁמַ֥ע אַבְרָהָ֖ם בְּקֹלִ֑י וַיִּשְׁמֹר֙ מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֔י מִצְוֺתַ֖י חֻקּוֹתַ֥י וְתוֹרֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: because listened Abraham to my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

en.L: because Abraham listened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice and kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} charge, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws."
en.B: because Abraham did as I told him and guarded all I gave him to keep: {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teachings."
en.R: I will do this because Abraham obeyed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He kept all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws."

decisions.choice: my charge, commandments, statutes and laws: the language of the later Law
decisions.reason: These four words are the ones used for the Law given through Moses (Deuteronomy 11:1). Long before Sinai, Abraham is described as a man who kept all God asked of him; his obedience flowed from the faith of 15:6 and was shown above all in 22:12-18.

decisions.choice: laws: instructions (torot)
decisions.reason: The word (torah) is first of all instruction or teaching, a father's or a priest's guidance as well as a written law.

decisions.choice: my, me (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself, so "my" and "me" take the deity pronoun setting.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יִצְחָ֖ק בִּגְרָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt Isaac in Gerar.

en.L: So Isaac dwelt in Gerar.
en.B: So Isaac settled in Gerar.
en.R: So Isaac stayed in Gerar.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁאֲל֞וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ לְאִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא כִּ֤י יָרֵא֙ לֵאמֹ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֔י פֶּן־יַֽהַרְגֻ֜נִי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ עַל־רִבְקָ֔ה כִּֽי־טוֹבַ֥ת מַרְאֶ֖ה הִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: And asked [the] men of the place about his wife, and he said, my sister [is] she; for he was afraid to say, my wife, lest kill me [the] men of the place on account of Rebekah, for good of appearance [was] she.

en.L: And the men of the place asked about his wife, and he said, "She is my sister," for he was afraid to say, "My wife," [thinking], "lest the men of the place kill me on account of Rebekah," for she was beautiful in appearance.
en.B: When the local men asked about his wife, he answered, "She is my sister." He was afraid to say she was his wife, thinking, "They might kill me here for Rebekah's sake," for she was a lovely woman.
en.R: The men there asked Isaac about his wife. He said, "She is my sister." He was afraid to say, "She is my wife." He thought, "The men here might kill me so they can have Rebekah." She was very beautiful.

decisions.choice: she is my sister: the father's lie repeated
decisions.reason: Abraham said the same of Sarah, in Egypt (12:13) and here in Gerar (20:2). Sarah was in fact Abraham's half-sister (20:12); Rebekah was Isaac's cousin's daughter (24:15), so Isaac's words are simply untrue. The son repeats the father's fear.

decisions.choice: lest the men of the place kill me: Isaac's thought, given in his own words
decisions.reason: The narrator slips into Isaac's own words ("kill me") without a verb of thinking, as Hebrew often does.

decisions.choice: [thinking]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the verb of thinking so the shift to Isaac's words ("me") can be followed.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּ֣י אָֽרְכוּ־ל֥וֹ שָׁם֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וַיַּשְׁקֵ֗ף אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים בְּעַ֖ד הַֽחַלּ֑וֹן וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה יִצְחָק֙ מְצַחֵ֔ק אֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when had grown long to him there the days, and looked down Abimelech, king of [the] Philistines, through the window and saw, and behold, Isaac [was] playing with Rebekah his wife.

en.L: And when he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down through the window and saw, and look, Isaac was playing with Rebekah his wife.
en.B: After Isaac had lived there for some time, Abimelech king of the Philistines happened to look down from a window, and there was Isaac, embracing his wife Rebekah.
en.R: Isaac stayed there a long time. One day Abimelech, the king of the Philistines, looked down from a window. He saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah the way a husband does with his wife.

decisions.choice: Isaac was playing (metsaheq): a pun on Isaac's name
decisions.reason: The verb (tsachaq) is the root of the name Isaac (yitschaq), "he laughs" (17:17-19; 21:6). Here it means the play of lovers, enough to show Abimelech that Rebekah was his wife. The same verb is used of Ishmael in 21:9 and of Potiphar's wife's charge in 39:14, 17.

decisions.choice: hugging and kissing ... the way a husband does with his wife
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why what Abimelech saw told him they were married (verse 9).

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְיִצְחָ֗ק וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַ֣ךְ הִנֵּ֤ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֙ הִ֔וא וְאֵ֥יךְ אָמַ֖רְתָּ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יִצְחָ֔ק כִּ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי פֶּן־אָמ֖וּת עָלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And summoned Abimelech Isaac and said, surely, behold, your wife [is] she; and how did you say, my sister [is] she? And said to him Isaac, for I said, lest I die on account of her.

en.L: And Abimelech called Isaac and said, "Look, she is surely your wife! How then could you say, 'She is my sister'?" And Isaac said to him, "Because I thought, 'I might die on account of her.'"
en.B: Abimelech sent for Isaac. "So she is your wife after all!" he said. "Why did you tell us she was your sister?" Isaac replied, "I was afraid someone would kill me for her."
en.R: So Abimelech called for Isaac and said, "She really is your wife! Why did you tell us she was your sister?" Isaac answered, "I was afraid someone would kill me to get her."

decisions.choice: I thought: literally "I said"
decisions.reason: "Say" is often used for what one says to oneself, that is, thinks.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ מַה־זֹּ֖את עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֑נוּ כִּ֠מְעַט שָׁכַ֞ב אַחַ֤ד הָעָם֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתֶּ֔ךָ וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ עָלֵ֖ינוּ אָשָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abimelech, what [is] this you have done to us? Almost lay one of the people with your wife, and you would have brought upon us guilt.

en.L: And Abimelech said, "What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us."
en.B: "What a thing to do to us!" Abimelech said. "It would have taken very little for one of the people to sleep with your wife, and you would have made us all guilty."
en.R: Abimelech said, "Why did you do this to us? One of my people could have slept with your wife. Then you would have made us guilty of a terrible sin."

decisions.choice: guilt (asham): wrong that needs to be made good
decisions.reason: The word means guilt that brings punishment and must be atoned for; later it names the guilt offering (Leviticus 5:15). Like the Abimelech of 20:9, the foreign king treats adultery as a grave sin before God, and the man of promise is the one rebuked.

decisions.choice: easily: literally "like a little"
decisions.reason: The phrase means "in a little while" or "almost": nothing stood in the way.

source.text: וַיְצַ֣ו אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הַנֹּגֵ֜עַ בָּאִ֥ישׁ הַזֶּ֛ה וּבְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded Abimelech all the people, saying, the one touching this man or his wife, surely will be put to death.

en.L: And Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, "Whoever touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death."
en.B: So Abimelech warned all his people, "Whoever touches this man or his wife must die."
en.R: Then Abimelech warned all his people, "If anyone hurts this man or touches his wife, that person will be put to death."

decisions.choice: touches: harms, or lays hands on
decisions.reason: The verb (naga) covers both harming a person and touching a woman sexually (20:6). Isaac is protected from harm and Rebekah from approach.

decisions.choice: hurts this man or touches his wife
decisions.reason: Readable gives each sense of "touch" its own verb (m1).

source.text: וַיִּזְרַ֤ע יִצְחָק֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֔וא וַיִּמְצָ֛א בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַהִ֖וא מֵאָ֣ה שְׁעָרִ֑ים וַֽיְבָרֲכֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And sowed Isaac in that land and found in that year a hundred measures, and blessed him YHWH.

en.L: And Isaac sowed in that land and reaped in that year a hundredfold; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed him.
en.B: Isaac sowed grain in that land, and that year it gave him a hundred times as much as he sowed. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} blessed him.
en.R: Isaac planted grain in that land. That year he gathered a hundred times as much as he planted, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed him.

decisions.choice: a hundredfold: literally "a hundred measures"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (she'arim, "measures") is unusual here. The Septuagint read the same letters with other vowels as se'orim, "barley". The Hebrew text is followed; either way the yield was a hundred times the seed.

decisions.choice: a hundredfold in a famine year: the LORD's blessing
decisions.reason: A hundredfold harvest was extraordinary anywhere, and this was a land in famine (verse 1). The promise of verse 3, "I will bless you", is kept at once.

decisions.choice: because
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link between the harvest and the LORD's blessing explicit.

source.text: וַיִּגְדַּ֖ל הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וְגָדֵ֔ל עַ֥ד כִּֽי־גָדַ֖ל מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And became great the man and went on going and growing great, until he became great exceedingly.

en.L: And the man became great, and he kept on growing greater until he became very great.
en.B: So Isaac grew great. He went on growing greater and greater until he was a man of enormous wealth.
en.R: Isaac became rich. He kept getting richer and richer until he was very wealthy.

decisions.choice: became great: rich and powerful
decisions.reason: The verb "be great" (gadal) is said three times: Isaac grows in wealth and standing, as God promised Abraham, "I will make your name great" (12:2; 24:35).

source.text: וַֽיְהִי־ל֤וֹ מִקְנֵה־צֹאן֙ וּמִקְנֵ֣ה בָקָ֔ר וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֑ה וַיְקַנְא֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And there were to him possessions of flock and possessions of herd and a great household, and envied him [the] Philistines.

en.L: And he had possessions of flocks and possessions of herds and a great household [of servants], and the Philistines envied him.
en.B: He came to own flocks and herds and a large household of slaves, and the Philistines envied him.
en.R: He had many sheep, goats and cattle, and many slaves. So the Philistines were jealous of him.

decisions.choice: a great household: a large body of servants
decisions.reason: The word (avuddah) means the people who work for a master, his household of servants (Job 1:3). In this setting they were owned workers, slaves.

source.text: וְכָל־הַבְּאֵרֹ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו בִּימֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יו סִתְּמ֣וּם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיְמַלְא֖וּם עָפָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And all the wells that had dug [the] servants of his father in [the] days of Abraham his father, stopped them up [the] Philistines and filled them [with] earth.

en.L: And all the wells that his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped up and filled with earth.
en.B: The Philistines had blocked every well that his father's slaves dug in Abraham's lifetime, filling them in with dirt.
en.R: The Philistines had filled with dirt all the wells that Abraham's slaves had dug while Abraham was alive.

decisions.choice: stopped up the wells: an act of hostility
decisions.reason: In dry country a well is life and a claim to the land around it (21:25-31). Filling in another man's wells was a way of driving him off.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: The household workers who dug Abraham's wells were owned people, so Balanced and Readable say "slaves", as for other owned workers in this translation.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־יִצְחָ֑ק לֵ֚ךְ מֵֽעִמָּ֔נוּ כִּֽי־עָצַֽמְתָּ־מִמֶּ֖נּוּ מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abimelech to Isaac, go from with us, for you have become mightier than us much.

en.L: And Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go away from us, for you have become much mightier than we."
en.B: Then Abimelech told Isaac, "Go and live somewhere away from us; you have grown much stronger than we are."
en.R: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go away from here. You are getting much stronger than we are."

decisions.choice: you have become much mightier than we: words that look ahead to Egypt
decisions.reason: The same verb (atsam) is used when Pharaoh says of Israel, "the people are more and mightier than we" (Exodus 1:9). The growth God gives makes the nations afraid.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם יִצְחָ֑ק וַיִּ֥חַן בְּנַֽחַל־גְּרָ֖ר וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went from there Isaac and camped in [the] valley of Gerar and dwelt there.

en.L: And Isaac went from there and camped in the valley of Gerar and dwelt there.
en.B: So Isaac moved away and pitched his camp in the Gerar valley, and he settled there.
en.R: So Isaac left. He set up his tents in the Gerar Valley and lived there.

decisions.choice: valley (nachal): a wadi
decisions.reason: A nachal is a valley with a stream bed that runs only in the rainy season. Water could often be found by digging in its bed.

source.text: וַיָּ֨שָׁב יִצְחָ֜ק וַיַּחְפֹּ֣ר׀אֶת־בְּאֵרֹ֣ת הַמַּ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ בִּימֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יו וַיְסַתְּמ֣וּם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֣וֹת אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶן֙ שֵׁמ֔וֹת כַּשֵּׁמֹ֕ת אֲשֶׁר־קָרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ן אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And again dug Isaac [the] wells of the water that they had dug in [the] days of Abraham his father, and had stopped them up [the] Philistines after [the] death of Abraham; and he called them names like the names that had called them his father.

en.L: And Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham; and he called their names by the names his father had called them.
en.B: Isaac dug out once more the water wells from his father Abraham's day, which the Philistines had choked up after Abraham's death, and he called them by the same names his father had used.
en.R: Isaac dug out again the wells from his father Abraham's time. The Philistines had filled them in after Abraham died. Isaac gave the wells the same names his father had given them.

decisions.choice: dug again: literally "returned and dug"
decisions.reason: "Return" with another verb means to do something again.

decisions.choice: the same names his father had used: renewing Abraham's claim
decisions.reason: Giving the wells their old names declared them Abraham's wells still, and so Isaac's by inheritance. Isaac walks in his father's steps.

source.text: וַיַּחְפְּר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי־יִצְחָ֖ק בַּנָּ֑חַל וַיִּ֨מְצְאוּ־שָׁ֔ם בְּאֵ֖ר מַ֥יִם חַיִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And dug [the] servants of Isaac in the valley and found there a well of living water.

en.L: And Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of living water.
en.B: Isaac's slaves dug in the valley and struck a well of fresh, flowing water.
en.R: Isaac's slaves dug in the valley and found a spring of fresh water.

decisions.choice: living water: fresh water that flows
decisions.reason: "Living water" is water from a spring, always fresh and moving, unlike water standing in a cistern. The prophets use it as a picture of God himself (Jeremiah 2:13).

source.text: וַיָּרִ֜יבוּ רֹעֵ֣י גְרָ֗ר עִם־רֹעֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק לֵאמֹ֖ר לָ֣נוּ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵֽׁם־הַבְּאֵר֙ עֵ֔שֶׂק כִּ֥י הִֽתְעַשְּׂק֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And quarreled [the] herdsmen of Gerar with [the] herdsmen of Isaac, saying, to us [is] the water. And he called [the] name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.

en.L: And the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, "The water is ours." And he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.
en.B: But the herdsmen of Gerar argued with Isaac's herdsmen, insisting, "This water belongs to us." So he named the well Esek, "Dispute", because of the dispute they had raised with him.
en.R: But the men who took care of the animals in Gerar argued with Isaac's men. They said, "This water belongs to us!" So Isaac named the well Esek, which means "arguing," because they had argued with him.

decisions.choice: Esek: "dispute"
decisions.reason: The name Esek and the verb that explains it (hit'asseqi, "they contended") come from the same root. Each well in this chapter is named for what happened at it.

decisions.choice: "Dispute" (B); which means "arguing" (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the name so the reason makes sense (m1).

source.text: וַֽיַּחְפְּרוּ֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וַיָּרִ֖יבוּ גַּם־עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמָ֖הּ שִׂטְנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they dug another well, and they quarreled also over it; and he called its name Sitnah.

en.L: And they dug another well, and they quarreled over it also; and he called its name Sitnah.
en.B: They dug a second well, and there was a quarrel over that one too, so he named it Sitnah, "Hostility".
en.R: Then they dug another well, and the men of Gerar argued about that one too. So Isaac named it Sitnah, which means "enemies."

decisions.choice: Sitnah: "hostility" or "accusation"
decisions.reason: The name comes from the root satan, to oppose or accuse, from which the word "satan", "adversary", is formed (Numbers 22:22; Job 1:6).

decisions.choice: "Hostility" (B); which means "enemies" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning of the name is given as with Esek (verse 20).

source.text: וַיַּעְתֵּ֣ק מִשָּׁ֗ם וַיַּחְפֹּר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וְלֹ֥א רָב֖וּ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ רְחֹב֔וֹת וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־עַתָּ֞ה הִרְחִ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה לָ֖נוּ וּפָרִ֥ינוּ בָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he moved from there and dug another well, and not they quarreled over it; and he called its name Rehoboth and said, for now has made room YHWH for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.

en.L: And he moved on from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it; and he called its name Rehoboth, and said, "For now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land."
en.B: He moved on from there and dug yet another well, and this time no one quarreled over it. He named it Rehoboth, "Open Spaces", saying, "Now at last {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made space for us, and we will be fruitful in the land."
en.R: Isaac moved on and dug another well, and no one argued about it. So he named it Rehoboth, which means "lots of room." He said, "Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given us plenty of space. We will grow and do well in this land."

decisions.choice: Rehoboth: "wide places", "room"
decisions.reason: The name and the verb hirchiv, "he has made room", come from the same root. Isaac does not fight for the wells; he moves on until God gives him room.

decisions.choice: we will be fruitful in the land: the blessing of creation
decisions.reason: "Be fruitful" is the blessing of 1:28 and 9:1 and the promise to Abraham (17:6). Isaac sees it coming true.

decisions.choice: "Open Spaces" (B); which means "lots of room" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning of the name is given as with Esek (verse 20).

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went up from there [to] Beersheba.

en.L: And he went up from there to Beersheba.
en.B: From there he went up to Beersheba.
en.R: Then Isaac went up to Beersheba.

decisions.choice: Beersheba: Abraham's well
decisions.reason: Abraham had dug a well here and made a treaty with Abimelech (21:25-33). It lay on the southern edge of the land, later its southern limit ("from Dan to Beersheba", Judges 20:1).

source.text: וַיֵּרָ֨א אֵלָ֤יו יְהוָה֙ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֕י אֱלֹהֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יךָ אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּֽי־אִתְּךָ֣ אָנֹ֔כִי וּבֵֽרַכְתִּ֨יךָ֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֔ בַּעֲב֖וּר אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And appeared to him YHWH in that night and said, I [am the] God of Abraham your father; do not fear, for with you [am] I, and I will bless you and I will multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham my servant.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him that night and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you, and I will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant."
en.B: That night {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Isaac. "I am your father Abraham's God," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "You have nothing to fear, because I am with you. For the sake of Abraham {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant I will bless you and make your descendants many."
en.R: That night {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Isaac and said, "I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, because I am with you. I will bless you and give you many descendants. I will do this because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Abraham."

decisions.choice: the God of Abraham your father: God names himself by his bond with a man
decisions.reason: This is the first time God calls himself "the God of" a person. The title grows: "the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac" (28:13), and finally "the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob" (Exodus 3:6).

decisions.choice: for the sake of Abraham my servant: blessing passed on through a faithful father
decisions.reason: "My servant" is a title of honor, later given to Moses (Numbers 12:7) and David (2 Samuel 7:5). Isaac is blessed for his father's sake, as verse 5 has said.

decisions.choice: "I am your father Abraham's God," he said
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the speech first, with "he said" in the deity pronoun setting.

source.text: וַיִּ֧בֶן שָׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ וַיִּקְרָא֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וַיֶּט־שָׁ֖ם אָהֳל֑וֹ וַיִּכְרוּ־שָׁ֥ם עַבְדֵי־יִצְחָ֖ק בְּאֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he built there an altar and called on [the] name of YHWH, and pitched there his tent; and dug there [the] servants of Isaac a well.

en.L: And he built an altar there and called on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and pitched his tent there; and Isaac's servants dug a well there.
en.B: Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He set up his tent there, and his slaves started digging a well.
en.R: Isaac built an altar there and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He set up his tents there, and his slaves dug a well.

decisions.choice: called on the name of the LORD: worshiped the LORD
decisions.reason: As with Abraham (12:8; 13:4; 21:33), calling on God's name means prayer and worship at the altar. Altar, tent and well: Isaac makes his home where God met him.

decisions.choice: dug (karah): a different verb for digging
decisions.reason: The verb (karah) is not the one used for the earlier wells (chafar); it is also used for digging a grave or a pit. The well is finished in verse 32.

decisions.choice: worshiped
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the idiom (m1).

source.text: וַאֲבִימֶ֕לֶךְ הָלַ֥ךְ אֵלָ֖יו מִגְּרָ֑ר וַאֲחֻזַּת֙ מֵֽרֵעֵ֔הוּ וּפִיכֹ֖ל שַׂר־צְבָאֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath his friend, and Phicol [the] commander of his army.

en.L: And Abimelech went to him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his friend and Phicol the commander of his army.
en.B: Then Abimelech came out from Gerar to see him, together with his counselor Ahuzzath and Phicol, his army commander.
en.R: One day Abimelech came from Gerar to see Isaac. Ahuzzath, his adviser, and Phicol, the commander of his army, came with him.

decisions.choice: his friend: a royal title, the king's adviser
decisions.reason: "The king's friend" was an office at court, a trusted counselor (2 Samuel 15:37; 1 Kings 4:5).

decisions.choice: Phicol the commander of his army: the name of chapter 21
decisions.reason: A Phicol was with Abimelech when he made a treaty with Abraham (21:22). The name may have passed to a successor, or have been a title.

decisions.choice: counselor (B), adviser (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the title (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ יִצְחָ֔ק מַדּ֖וּעַ בָּאתֶ֣ם אֵלָ֑י וְאַתֶּם֙ שְׂנֵאתֶ֣ם אֹתִ֔י וַתְּשַׁלְּח֖וּנִי מֵאִתְּכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Isaac, why have you come to me, and you hated me and sent me away from with you?

en.L: And Isaac said to them, "Why have you come to me, since you hate me and have sent me away from you?"
en.B: Isaac asked them, "Why have you come to me? You hated me and drove me away."
en.R: Isaac said to them, "Why have you come here? You hated me and made me leave your land."

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ רָא֣וֹ רָאִינוּ֮ כִּֽי־הָיָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה׀עִמָּךְ֒ וַנֹּ֗אמֶר תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א אָלָ֛ה בֵּינוֹתֵ֖ינוּ בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְנִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, clearly we have seen that has been YHWH with you; and we said, let there be, please, an oath between us, between us and you; and let us make a covenant with you,

en.L: And they said, "We have clearly seen that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been with you. So we said, 'Let there be an oath between us, between us and you,' and let us make a covenant with you,
en.B: They replied, "It is plain to us that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been with you. So we thought, 'Let the two sides, we and you, be bound by an oath.' We want to make a covenant with you,
en.R: They answered, "We can see that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with you. So we want both of us to make a promise with an oath. Let us make a covenant with you.

decisions.choice: the LORD has been with you: outsiders see the promise kept
decisions.reason: God promised, "I will be with you" (verse 3), and the king who drove Isaac away now says it is so. The same was said to Abraham (21:22).

decisions.choice: an oath (alah): a sworn pledge with a curse
decisions.reason: The word is an oath that calls down a curse on the one who breaks it; with the covenant it binds both sides.

decisions.choice: make a covenant: literally "cut a covenant"
decisions.reason: The usual idiom for making a covenant, as in 15:18 and 21:27.

source.text: אִם־תַּעֲשֵׂ֨העִמָּ֜נוּ רָעָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א נְגַֽעֲנ֔וּךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֤ינוּ עִמְּךָ֙ רַק־ט֔וֹב וַנְּשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ֖ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם אַתָּ֥ה עַתָּ֖ה בְּר֥וּךְ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: that you will do with us harm, just as not we touched you, and just as we have done with you only good, and sent you away in peace; you now [are the] blessed of YHWH.

en.L: that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you, and as we have done to you nothing but good and sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: that you will not harm us, since we did not touch you; we did you nothing but good and sent you off in peace. You are the one whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed now."
en.R: Promise that you will not hurt us. We did not hurt you. We were always good to you, and we let you leave in peace. Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed you."

decisions.choice: that you will do us no harm: the form of an oath
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is "if you do us harm", the first half of an oath whose curse is left unsaid: "(may this happen to you) if you harm us". It means "you will not harm us".

decisions.choice: we did you nothing but good and sent you off in peace: their own account
decisions.reason: They had driven Isaac away (verse 16) and stopped his wells (verses 15, 20-21); they put the best face on it. Isaac does not argue, and makes peace (verses 30-31), as one through whom blessing is to reach the nations (verse 4).

decisions.choice: will do us no harm / will not harm us
decisions.reason: The oath form is given in its plain meaning (m1).

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ וַיִּשְׁתּֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made for them a feast, and they ate and drank.

en.L: And he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
en.B: Isaac prepared a banquet for them, and they ate and drank.
en.R: Isaac made a big meal for them, and they ate and drank.

decisions.choice: a feast: a covenant meal
decisions.reason: Eating together sealed a covenant; those who shared a meal were bound in peace (31:54; Exodus 24:11).

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּשָּׁבְע֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ לְאָחִ֑יו וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֣ם יִצְחָ֔ק וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they rose early in the morning and swore, each to his brother; and sent them away Isaac, and they went from with him in peace.

en.L: And they rose early in the morning and swore an oath, each man to his brother; and Isaac sent them off, and they went from him in peace.
en.B: They were up early the next morning and bound themselves by oath to each other. Isaac then sent them on their way, and they parted from him in peace.
en.R: Early the next morning they each made a promise with an oath to the other. Then Isaac sent them home, and they left in peace.

decisions.choice: each man to his brother: to one another
decisions.reason: "Brother" in this phrase means simply the other party.

decisions.choice: swore an oath (nishba): the root of Shibah
decisions.reason: The verb "swear" comes from the same root as the number seven (sheva) and as the name the well receives the same day (verse 33).

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י יִצְחָ֔ק וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ עַל־אֹד֥וֹת הַבְּאֵ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑רוּ וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ מָצָ֥אנוּ מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on that day, and came [the] servants of Isaac and told him about the well that they had dug, and said to him, we have found water.

en.L: And on that same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had dug, and said to him, "We have found water."
en.B: That same day Isaac's slaves came to report on the well they had been digging. "We have struck water!" they told him.
en.R: That same day Isaac's slaves came and told him about the well they had been digging. They said, "We have found water!"

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ שִׁבְעָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֤ן שֵׁם־הָעִיר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he called it Shibah; therefore [the] name of the city [is] Beersheba until this day.

en.L: And he called it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
en.B: He named it Shibah, "Oath", and that is why the town is called Beersheba to this day.
en.R: Isaac named the well Shibah, which means "oath." That is why the town there is still called Beersheba, which means "well of the oath."

decisions.choice: Shibah ... Beersheba: "oath" ... "well of the oath"
decisions.reason: Shibah sounds like the words for oath and for seven. Abraham had already named the place Beersheba after his oath with Abimelech and the seven lambs (21:28-31). Isaac's new well and new oath renew the name, as he renewed his father's well names (verse 18).

decisions.choice: "Oath" (B); which means "oath" ... "well of the oath" (R)
decisions.reason: The meanings are given so the reader can see why the name fits (m1).

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י עֵשָׂו֙ בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וַיִּקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ אֶת־יְהוּדִ֔ית בַּת־בְּאֵרִ֖י הַֽחִתִּ֑י וְאֶת־בָּ֣שְׂמַ֔ת בַּת־אֵילֹ֖ן הַֽחִתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And was Esau a son of forty years, and he took [as] wife Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite.

en.L: And Esau was forty years old, and he took as wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
en.B: At forty, Esau took two wives, both of them Hittites: Judith, daughter of Beeri, and Basemath, daughter of Elon.
en.R: When Esau was forty years old, he married two Hittite women. One was Judith, the daughter of Beeri. The other was Basemath, the daughter of Elon.

decisions.choice: forty years old: the age at which Isaac married
decisions.reason: Isaac married Rebekah at forty (25:20). Abraham had taken great care that Isaac's wife should not be a Canaanite (24:3); Esau marries two.

decisions.choice: Judith and Basemath: names given differently in 36:2-3
decisions.reason: The list of Esau's wives in 36:2-3 names Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, Oholibamah, and Basemath daughter of Ishmael (called Mahalath in 28:9). The two lists come from different records, and women sometimes bore more than one name; the Hebrew of each passage is followed as it stands.

source.text: וַתִּהְיֶ֖יןָ מֹ֣רַת ר֑וּחַ לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּלְרִבְקָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they were bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.

en.L: And they were a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.
en.B: These wives made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah.
en.R: Esau's wives made Isaac and Rebekah very unhappy.

decisions.choice: bitterness of spirit: deep grief
decisions.reason: The phrase means lasting grief and vexation. It prepares for Rebekah's words in 27:46 and for Jacob being sent to find a wife among their own people (28:1-2).
